protocol: plan docs/plans/2026-10-18-confirmation-3.md §0 (copied, not reopened; §0.10 allows the review only to tighten §0.4) and §0.13; runner nano/confirm3.py generate / manifest / score, bound with this file and frozen.py by the registration commit
frozen_from: runs/c2-confirm2/frozen.py (sha e772bd6e...) = E002b, promoted 2026-10-16 as the dev incumbent: 4 Luna samples, then a Sol judge picks among the distinct public-green files (one green: submitted as is; none: a Luna repair). It passed C2-LOOK1. It was superseded as the dev incumbent on 2026-10-20 by E007 (Sol-directed repair; fresh dev confirmation +17.1 pp all-pass vs E002). E007 is not the candidate because its one permitted look (C2-LOOK2, 10-21) was invalid (one hidden-test-name hit), so under plan §0.1 the candidate is E002.
candidate_rule: look 2 not a valid PASS for E007; candidate E002
branch_caps: judge (>= 2 distinct public-green files): 4 Luna + 1 Sol; one-green: 4 Luna; no-green-repair: 4 Luna + 1 Luna. Never more than 5 calls, at most 1 Sol.
claim_wording: At an equal invocation cap of 5 model calls per task, a two-model harness (at most 5 calls per task: 4 Luna samples, then either 1 Sol judge call at medium effort or 1 Luna repair) produces working software (every hidden test passes) more often than Luna alone in a plain repair loop (D, at most 5 Luna calls) and in best-of-5 with public-test selection (B). Not cost- or token-matched: Sol is a stronger model from the same vendor, X used about 4.6x D's tokens on dev, and no cost-matched control (e.g. D plus one Sol call) is run. Calls and tokens by lane are reported beside the claim.

decision_rule.authority: nano/confirm3.py decide() over runs/c2-confirm3/pooled-summary.json (a2d lift pool of both replicate ledgers) and the per-(task, arm, replicate) voids
decision_rule.SUPPORTED: X vs D and X vs B both Supported by the controller rule on complete tuples (ci_low > 0, lift >= +10 pp, >= 10 families, discordance) AND, over every planned (task, replicate) with voids imputed worst-case (void X = fail, void D/B = pass), lift >= +10 pp and whole-family bootstrap ci_low > 0 vs both
decision_rule.RULED OUT: X vs D RuledOut on complete tuples (ci_high < +10 pp) AND best-case imputed (void X = pass, void D = fail) point and bootstrap ci_high both < +10 pp
decision_rule.IntegrityReview: any hidden-test name hit (pooled summary, either replicate's own summary, or a failed first attempt's prompts), tool events > 0.5% of a replicate's invocations (the largest of the submission, invocation-record and recount sums, a failed first attempt's calls included), a failed first attempt with any unauditable call (no ledger, an unparsable line, a call started but never recorded, a prompt without its record, a call without its transcript) or with its own rate above 0.5%, a malformed replicate summary, or the controller's own IntegrityReview
decision_rule.Invalid: void tuples > 5% of all (task, arm, replicate) tuples, the controller's excluded-share guard or own Invalid, an aborted run, or a missing or malformed pooled summary or comparison (a missing or malformed replicate summary is IntegrityReview; an aborted generation is a failed attempt: failure_policy)
decision_rule.void tuple: void or unscored submission; any tool event on the submission or on any of its invocation records (lane calls included), by the binary's count or by the runner's own recount of the transcript; any invocation without a --json transcript carrying the stderr marker (a legacy text transcript is void); a call whose turn started without the host-off notice before it; recorded invocations != the submission's claimed count; a malformed record; all tuples of a replicate with an unparsable ledger line, a changed codex fingerprint or a missing bracket record

spend.requires: confirmation-2 sealed (runs/c2-confirm2/sealed-sha256.txt), the authoring pipeline drained, codex = the registered fingerprint
spend.latency_go: median of 3 canary coding calls on the coder lane through `a2d lift run` <= 45 s, plus one canary call per registered lane; every lane needs at least one successful call whose transcript the runner recounts at 0 events with the host-off notice; all with 0 tool events and the canary secret in no response
spend.replicate_2: a later UTC day than replicate 1's generation

failure_policy: each replicate is attempted once (attempt record before any model call); a deferral is not an attempt; a generation that fails before generation_complete may be relaunched once with the same seed in its own dir, logged; a second failure ends confirmation-3 as not run

instrument.provider: c2-web-provider merged into main at c14956a0 (branch head ecbb9611, including the §0.14 cwd/CODEX_HOME uniqueness fix 36bea1e1), plus 19d6e1e6 (§0.16): no web search, isolated CODEX_HOME per call, tool features disabled including code_mode_host (no MCP tool exists), --json allowlist tool counting with one fixed pre-turn host-off notice exempt, failed-call transcripts (plan §0.13); the runner recounts every transcript with its own port of the detector and requires the notice before every turn
instrument.launch: each generate runs detached (own session, caffeinate) from the queue runner; the controller is built before the preflight, and the suite hash and the crates binding are checked before the attempt record
instrument.binding: the controller refuses to run or score if crates/, Cargo.toml or Cargo.lock differ from the registration commit

power: docs/experiments/analysis/c3_power.py (dev summaries only): P(RULED OUT | 0) = 0.91; P(SUPPORTED) = 0.14 / 0.33 / 0.47 / 0.96 at +7.1 / +8.9 / +10 / +15 pp
expected_spend_per_replicate: about 1.6k invocations, Luna and Sol together (confirmation-2: 1,618 and 1,617), of which about 1.5k Luna
disclosures: Authorship: the tasks were authored blind by Sol (gpt-6.1-sol, high) and audited by an independent Sol solve (medium); a Sol judge lane in the candidate is an author-judge alignment. The claim stays narrow, to this authoring distribution.

Mid-authoring pipeline fixes (plan §0.13): the command scan's prose false positive (ecfb1c65), the retry codex-home reset (17da7217) and the mutants-directory check that allows non-source extras (99890cd2). Jobs before 08:00 UTC 10-19 ran under the earlier pipeline commit.

Step order (plan §0.13): the step-5 audit ran from the provider branch (2830f5ba, 3ca9102b) before main merged the provider (c14956a0, 10-21); certification checks that each audit head contains the provider commit.
Audit round 1's 4 voids were an instrument fault (§0.14: two concurrent calls sharing a cwd and CODEX_HOME), fixed before registration (36bea1e1); the 4 tasks were re-audited and solved in round 2.

Provenance (registration reviews): the last validation (10-21) built its own controller and recorded its git head and binary sha256; certification requires that record. The audit runs recorded binary sha256 790bcf91... at heads 2830f5ba and 3ca9102b, which debug builds cannot reproduce byte for byte, so the audit's evidence is re-derived without that binary: an independent sandboxed oracle (python + rustc) re-scored every final-round submission (144/144 agree) and the runner's own detector port recounted their 144 transcripts (0 events, 0 missing); certification requires both. The audit's launch isolation (its CODEX_HOME and environment) is not independently re-verifiable; it bears on which tasks were certified, not on the arm comparison.

Compile-time file reads (registration reviews): the validator's API-surface check compiled model-written Rust outside the sandbox, and it refuses to run once a registration exists. A counts-only lexical scan (c3_channel_audit.py: comments stripped, aliased imports, bare macro names, #[path] and mod loaders) of the suite, the authoring tree and both audit runs found 0 reading macros, 0 loaders and 0 sealed-path mentions (channel-audit.json). A lexical scan is not a proof: macro-identifier indirection through a user macro is not detected.

Instrument errors count as tool events (fail closed): codex `error` items (except the one pre-turn host-off notice), top-level `error` events and `turn.failed` count, so an API failure voids its tuple and a burst could reach IntegrityReview. Measured: 'model at capacity' failures in 4 of 11,260 Luna dev calls (about 0.04%) and 1 Sol judge call in the 44-call rehearsal 4 (run alongside other load; it voided its tuple, 2 events); timeouts in about 0.5% of calls, which keep their transcript and count no event. At about one capacity failure per 1.6k-call replicate, crossing 0.5% (more than 8 events) needs a burst of 5 or more; other Luna and Sol work is held during the windows. A failed X judge call voids an X tuple (imputed as an X fail).

MCP tools (plan §0.16): dev, the dev-holdout looks and the audit ran with codex's built-in MCP resource tools available (a Luna coder occasionally listed empty resources; such tuples were voided there too). Confirmation-3 runs with code_mode_host off, so no MCP tool exists; codex then emits one fixed pre-turn notice, exempt from the count, whose presence the runner requires on every call. Symmetric across arms; injected instructions unchanged.

Relaunch: a first attempt that dies with calls in flight leaves unmatched invocation_started records, which are unauditable and make the run IntegrityReview; the one relaunch therefore rescues only failures without calls in flight (fail closed).

Operations during the spend windows: generation runs detached; other Luna work (phase-B rounds, dev runs) is held while a replicate generates; codex is not upgraded (a fingerprint change voids the replicate).
Injected context: codex 0.162 injects its 4 bundled skills (~7.3k chars) and multi-agent role text (~2.8k) that no switch removes; identical in every arm, no task information.

Instrument versus dev: the dev and dev-holdout estimates were measured with web search open (unused), plugins and user skills loaded; confirmation-3 runs with them off (C2-WEB, C2-MCP, plan §0.13). Symmetric across arms.
Integrity policy: tuple-level voids with worst-case imputation, weaker than confirmation-2's any-event amendment but conservative for the claim; IntegrityReview above 0.5% tool events per replicate.

Voids are imputed on the CI as well as the point (early reviews, plan §0.13): SUPPORTED needs the controller rule on complete tuples AND the worst-case imputed point >= +10 pp AND the worst-case imputed whole-family bootstrap ci_low > 0 vs both comparators; RULED OUT needs the controller RuledOut AND the best-case imputed ci_high < +10 pp. The bootstrap is the controller's (ported; exact on 4 dev comparisons).
Codex version: --json transcripts carry no banner, so the binary is pinned by a sha256 fingerprint bracketing each replicate; a change voids that replicate's tuples.

Spent sets: confirmation-2 (IntegrityReview, web search in arm B); its scored data stays sealed until this decision and is then reported descriptively. Dev-holdout looks: look 1 (E002, PASS) and look 2 (E007, invalid: one coincidental hidden-test name in a judge prompt, echoed from a Luna draft).
Possible model drift between the dev runs (10-15 to 10-23) and the spend days.

SPEC.md was kept byte-identical through authoring (Sol's suggestion #22 not adopted); the limits disclosed in §0.11 and the step-5 tooling choices of §0.12 apply (a void audit is no information and is re-audited once; a repair may change only the requirements, never the hidden tests, and must pass validation and similarity again; one task was so repaired).
Authoring sandbox: a copied `security` binary can list the world-readable system keychain's metadata (no secrets); the login keychain file is unreadable (§0.12).

The controller's own excluded-share guard (5% of (task, replicate) pairs, any arm void excludes the pair) is stricter than §0.13's 5% of (task, arm, replicate) tuples and also applies; c3_power assumed no voids, so the best-case RULED OUT guard lowers P(RULED OUT | 0) below 0.91.
Latency go/no-go probes are model calls (3 Luna canary coding calls plus 1 per registered lane, per spend attempt) made before the attempt record; they count toward the daily cap.

Launch isolation before each replicate (§0.10): no codex context in any ancestor of the temp root; every call's auth-only CODEX_HOME under the holdout dir (A2D_CODEX_HOME_ROOT); a canary preflight through the real provider on every lane (the secret in no response, 0 tool events); the codex fingerprint.

Detector inventory (codex 0.162 exec item types): command_execution, file_change, mcp_tool_call, web_search and collab_tool_call have live positive controls on every lane (controls.json), each with code_mode_host switched back on for that control (it hosts shell and MCP); the shipped call's one pre-turn host-off `error` notice is checked live as present and not counted, and every other `error` item is counted (unit test); todo_list could not be triggered in exec mode even with every feature on and is covered by the allowlist only; image tools have no exec item type and are disabled by feature flags.

Exposure policy: no confirmation-3 content was shown to any proposer, harness or operator. Task content exists only under the holdout dir; only counts, opaque ids and gateway booleans left it (diagnostics of 2026-10-19 printed fixed vocabularies only). A task found exposed is excluded before the hash; none was.

Hidden-name exposure: the IntegrityReview rule counts any hidden-test name found as an identifier in any prompt, including model-written code that a later prompt carries (X's judge prompts carry Luna's files; D's repair prompts carry its previous attempt; B's prompts carry none). The observed base rate is about 1 coincidental hit per 2-3k such prompts (0 in 12,356 cycle-2 dev prompts, 0 in look 1 and in the confirmation-3 audits, and 1 in look 2, where a Luna draft named something exactly like a hidden test). With about 340 such prompts over two replicates, that is a rough 10-15% chance of an IntegrityReview with no leak. Confirmation-3's naming conventions may differ from the suites behind that rate. The rule is not narrowed (plan §0.10).

The frozen candidate is not the strongest harness found on dev: the dev incumbent E007 beat E002 there (+7.1 and +17.1 pp all-pass over two replicates), but its only permitted dev-holdout look was invalid. E007's advantage on this confirmation distribution is unmeasured; this test says nothing about E007.
